text:
ali: noticed a repeating tail-latency pattern on apac-edge rack q4 starting ~22:10 UTC. p95 jumps to ~900ms for ~30-40s every 4-5 minutes.

mei: i've got the trace. It lines up with a tenant (tenant-reco) kicking off periodic large-batch reranks. NVSwitch and NIC TX spike together.

ops-bot: [ALERT] apac-edge/rack-q4: p95 > 800ms (infra.latency.p95)

sam: any MIG/non-MIG mixing on q4? that usually makes fabric arbitration worse when one job is heavy.

mei: q4 is mixed; we tried to consolidate last month but a few legacy non-mig jobs remain pinned.

ali: pasted a metric snapshot from 22:12:
```
2026-05-06T22:12:04Z rack=q4 node=host12 gpu0 util=94 nvlink=81Gb/s nic_tx=3.7GB/s
2026-05-06T22:12:04Z rack=q4 node=host12 gpu1 util=28 nvlink=9Gb/s nic_tx=0.2GB/s
2026-05-06T22:12:04Z rack=q4 node=host13 gpu0 util=91 nvlink=79Gb/s nic_tx=3.4GB/s
```

sam: classic bimodal util + host tx. tenant-reco's rerank shards are saturating NVLink and pushing host egress when they write tmp checkpoints.

mei: immediate options: 1) soft reschedule tenant-reco batch pods off q4 to ephemeral-burst, 2) set per-tenant nvlink/nic quota, 3) temporarily disable non-MIG workloads on q4. Which has lowest blast radius?

ali: (1) lowest risk. do we have an ephemeral pool with free capacity in apac-edge?

ops-bot: cluster status: ephemeral-burst-apac has 6% spare GPU capacity currently.

sam: small risk of moving causing cold starts, but benefit should be quick. do a dry-run first to show PDB impact.

mei: running dry-run: tenant-reco has 5 batch replicas, 2 respect PDB. live reschedule with 90s grace should move 3 immediately.

ali: go ahead, run `apictl placement reschedule --rack q4 --label job=rerank --to-pool ephemeral-burst-apac --grace 90s` and watch p95. add a temp placement tag `placement.sensitive=true` for low-latency pods so new batch pods don't land on affected racks.

ops-bot: user mei invoked placement reschedule (job=rerank) on rack q4

mei: reschedule running: 3/5 moved, 1 blocking on PDB, 1 in progress. p95 dropped to ~240ms after two moves. :thumbsup:

sam: nice. Mei, can you also push a temporary nvlink asymmetry alert rule (gpu.util.stddev > 0.25) so we catch next time sooner? 

mei: will do. also logging an action to consider stricter pool isolation for tenant-reco if this repeats (owner: ali).

ali: long-term we should avoid mixing non-MIG with latency-sensitive pods on same NVSwitch domain. I'll add a card to infra backlog to enforce NVSwitch-aware placement and to surface nvlink per-tenant on console.

ops-bot: reminder: please file incident summary in #incidents when stable.

mei: reschedule complete; p95 stable ~200ms for last 10m. I'll leave temp placement rule for 45m, then revert.

sam: thanks. if we see recurrence consider a temporary dedicated carve for tenant-reco during their rerank windows as an escalation.

ali: agreed. closing loop after incident note. thanks team.
